question: Do public Quezon and DENR records identify which Dagatan Lake the 2024 CALABARZON wetland roadmap intended, and whether it is Lake Pagatan?

sources.observedText: Under Municipality of San Antonio, the provincial directory describes boating down the man-made Dagatan Lake and lists Dagatan Lake as a point of interest.
limits: The page provides no coordinates, shoreline, area, BMB site code, or explicit equivalence to Lake Pagatan.
Tourism-directory naming does not establish current waterbody geometry or fish presence.

sources.provider: DENR-FASPS library; Dagatan Lake Watershed Management Plan annex
sources.observedText: The plan identifies a 2 ha Dagatan Lake in Sitio Busal, Barangay Ibabang Palale, Tayabas City, Quezon.
sources.access: Official PDF text view read on 2026-11-01 at printed pages 2-3; source publication age and proposed protected-area statement do not establish present status.
limits: The 2 ha figure conflicts with the BMB atlas/inventory's 24.38 ha Dagat Dagatan Lake row; neither is current geometry.
The plan's common-name fish mentions are not used here as verified scientific taxa, present occurrences, or a complete list.

sources.observedText: The 2024-2029 roadmap lists Dagatan Lake and Pagatan Lake separately in Quezon Province but gives neither a municipality nor a site code.
sources.access: Official page search-index text reviewed; direct page fetch returned HTTP 403.
limits: The list does not map either phrase to a municipality or the BMB atlas row.
The headline says 30 wetlands while the printed name phrases count 31; this review does not reconcile the denominator.

established: An official Quezon provincial page names a man-made Dagatan Lake in San Antonio.
A DENR-hosted watershed plan describes another Dagatan Lake in Ibabang Palale, Tayabas City, at a historical 2 ha.
BMB's 2014 atlas and 2019 inventory list Dagat Dagatan Lake in Tayabas City (24.38 ha) and Lake Pagatan in San Antonio (3.22 ha) as separate rows.
crosswalkAssessment.unresolved: The official Quezon page does not state whether San Antonio's man-made Dagatan Lake is the BMB Lake Pagatan. The 2024 roadmap's Dagatan Lake phrase could refer to the Tayabas locality, the San Antonio locality, or another mapped feature; its separate Pagatan Lake phrase is also not tied to a site code. Do not merge or assign either roadmap phrase until an authoritative municipality/site-code crosswalk is found.
crosswalkAssessment.denominator: The official roadmap headline of 30 wetlands versus 31 visible name phrases remains unresolved; no duplicate or missing feature is inferred.

nextAction: Continue independent locality-resolved CALABARZON source review. For the wetland roadmap crosswalk, seek public DENR or Quezon LGU maps, site-code tables, or project records that distinguish San Antonio Dagatan from San Antonio Pagatan and identify the intended Tayabas entry. Do not send a request without Joseph's authorization.
